Q. An ice box is made of wood 1.75 cm thick lined inside with cork 2 cm thick. If the temperature of inner surface of the cork is steady at 0C and that of the outer surface of the wood is steady at 12C, what is the temperature of the interface? The thermal conductivity of wood is five time that of cork.
Temperature of outer part of wood () = 12C
We know that for steady flow of heat,
Rate of flow of heat from wood = Rate of flow of heat from cork
Hence the temperature of the interface between wood and cork is 10.2°C.

Convection is the process of transfer of heat in fluids by means of the actual motion of heated particles from high temperature region to low temperature region. Heating of water, land

breezes, sea breezes, winds, etc. are some examples of convection. In convection, heated particles carry heat and move from the hotter region to the colder region, but the cold particles move in opposite directions. Convection is possible only in liquid and gas but not in solid and vacuum. There are two types of convection; natural convection and artificial convection.
[Fig;12.6 convection; forced convection and natural convection]

Natural or Free Convection; Natural convection is also called free convection. The primary circulation of the Earth's atmosphere causing daily weather results, land breezes, sea breezes, and trade winds are examples of natural convection. Natural convection is the most commonly brought about by local change in density which is ultimately associated with pressure difference or temperature difference between two regions of fluid. Buoyant force is responsible for movement of particles during natural convection, and it is impossible in gravity-free region.

Artificial or Forced Convection; If convection is carried out by maintaining pressure difference mechanically by a pump or a blower or by any means of externalaid then the convection is called artificial convection or forced convection. Pumping up the blood by the heart and its circulation through the different parts is an example of forced convection. This process keeps our body warm. Also, the use of fans to cool an electronic equipment using water heaters or geysers for instant heating of water are examples of forced convection.
